Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

---
name: continual-arc
description: Solve Continual-ARC grid puzzles; compare demos, manage attempt/demo costs, verify full-grid outputs, and format actions.
---

# Continual-ARC

1. Treat each instance as independent. Read the full grid, all demonstrations, and remaining attempt/demo budgets. Compare exact changed cells and dimensions; separate established transformations from plausible but unverified explanations.
2. Spend demo requests only when another pair can distinguish live hypotheses and its information is worth the cost. Respect the displayed demo cap. After an incorrect submission, discard or revise the rejected hypothesis specifically; do not repeat it or pivot to an unrelated guess. When feedback is only correct/incorrect, use it to test one evidence-based alternative, not to infer which individual edits were wrong.
3. For large grids, construct the candidate programmatically only as a private calculation aid: transcribe the input exactly, keep it immutable, apply the demonstrated rule, and verify the candidate against every demo with the same transformation before submitting. Check source and output dimensions, row lengths, values, and unchanged cells. A script result is not evidence the rule is correct; inspect the inferred operation and candidate explicitly.
4. Return exactly one supported action JSON on the last line. Submit a grid only when the rule and serialization are checked; request_demos only within the cap; use finish only after the instance is over. Never execute the puzzle action through shell or another tool.
